crm_notes: Company: developer tools startup building an IDE copilot embedded in a browser+desktop editor.
Primary workload: inline code completion + multi-line generative suggestions; short completions for UX and occasional longer refactors.
TTFT target: <40ms for single-line suggestions, aim 25-35ms in most hot paths; acceptable 40-60ms for multi-line blocks.
Jitter tolerance: prefer <10ms variance at 95th pct for token streaming; spikes above 80ms are user-visible and unacceptable.
Throughput: hundreds of concurrent developer sessions per cluster during peak; median request size ~20 tokens, tail up to 150 tokens.
Token budget strategy: per-session token budget for interactive assistants (150 tokens avg), backpressure when budget low with graceful degrade to prefix-only hints.
Streaming behavior: chunked token streaming preferred; small chunk sizes (4-8 tokens) for low perceived latency; want control over chunk interval and early-first-token delivery.
Backpressure & flow-control: editor will pause new keystroke inference during model-side backpressure; need deterministic signals for client to show 'loading' vs 'partial suggestion'.
Model/version pinning: must pin to specific code models per workspace; auto-fallback to quantized smaller model if dedicated capacity saturated.
Caching: strong interest in prefix/KV caching for autocomplete patterns across sessions and file-level caches to reduce latency and cost.
Cost sensitivity: mid-high; willing to pay for dedicated capacity to guarantee TTFT but want Optimize recommendations to tune batching and quantization.
Security: VPC + SSO required for internal teams; legal asks for data residency in US/EU and 90-day retention controls; KMS for keying.
POC ask: run a 2-week POC using Dedicated pool (pinned model), measure time-to-first-token, jitter (95/99pct), and effective token-cost per completion.
